source_observations.observation: Ordinary and continual deserving differ. Virāga has a member-specific replacement.
The substituted compound member requires the suffixal construction. Both affixes survive.

source_observations.locator: Kāśikā and Kaumudī at 5.1.66, frozen PG36 records
source_observations.observation: The former says ya and the latter specifies yat. The habitual qualification ends.
Three grammatical examples for the Vedic deserving relation.
Pātra admits both measure and vessel and the forms with ghan and yat.
Both alternatives for each of the two bases. Rule 70 transmits both to the rice example.
Ordered assignment. The supplement selects fitness for the corresponding activity.

source_observations.locator: Manusmṛti 8.128, GRETIL; compare Medhātithi at the same verse
source_observations.observation: Positive and negative accusatives plural have contrasting referents. The verse has pre-ca sandhi on the positive.
A tree suitable for a post and one suitable for a plough are distinguished. Accusative and genitive forms of the post adjective occur.
Neuter plural of names as objects of dadhire. Sāyaṇa expressly cites 5.1.71 and gha.

source_observations.locator: Śākala Ṛgveda 1.72.4 and 6, Pada and Sāyaṇa
source_observations.observation: The same masculine nominative plural denotes gods at 4 and qualified sacrificers at 6 on the commentator's interpretation.
Two free instrumentals plural and one compound-initial fee adjective.

source_observations.locator: Jayamaṅgalā at Bhaṭṭi 2.29, 1928, printed pp. 30–31, digital leaf 69 rev. 376713 (verse on 68)
source_observations.observation: Names 69 and 71. The compound receives a paraphrase with sages deserving dakṣiṇā; the two instrumentals are explained by sacrificial materials and the priestly activity.

source_observations.locator: Kālidāsa, Mālavikāgnimitra V, Sārasaka's dialogue and Sanskrit chāyā
source_observations.observation: The dialogue has a Middle Indic instrumental; the Sanskrit reading dakṣiṇyaiḥ is the edition's chāyā in note 3.

source_observations.locator: Vārttika as reported after 5.1.71, examples for place and priestly family
source_observations.observation: The action-qualified supplement supplies a place and a family, each explicitly distinct from the person examples preceding it.
